q: How much electricity does a VFD on a thermic fluid pump save in a textile processing house?
title: VFD on a thermopac pump: power saved
short: About 77,600 kWh a year, close to half the pump's power, in BEE's Pali report: a VFD trims a 23 kW thermic fluid pump from 120 to 96 m3 an hour. Cost Rs 1.75 lakh, saving Rs 3.57 lakh at Rs 4.60 a kWh, payback about 6 months (2010). CO2 falls about 52 t on today's grid.
audience: Pali and Balotra process houses running 10 or 20 lakh kcal an hour thermopacs for stenters and printing dryers

ul: The pump runs 24 hours to keep the fluid moving, so it is often the biggest single motor in a Pali process house: rated 20 or 30 kW, drawing 16 or 23 kW.
Stenters (rated 4 lakh kcal an hour, running near 3) and printing dryers take less heat than the thermopac can give, and their valves bypass hot fluid when a chamber is hot enough.
So the pump pushes more fluid than the load needs, all day. BEE found no VFD on any thermic fluid pump in Pali.
Now: 23 kW x 24 hours x 300 days = 165,600 kWh.
With the VFD and PLC: flow 120 to 96 m3 an hour, 80%. Pump power falls with the cube of flow, 0.8 x 0.8 x 0.8 = 0.51, so 84,787 kWh.
The drive itself uses about 3,232 kWh. Net saving 77,578 kWh, Rs 3.57 lakh.
Cost: Rs 1.5 lakh drive and controls, Rs 0.25 lakh fitting. One to two days of downtime.

sections.h: Two checks before you fit it
ul: Minimum flow: the heater coils need a minimum fluid velocity or the oil cracks and cokes. Get that figure from the thermopac maker and set it as the drive's floor.
The cube rule works when pipe friction is most of the pump's head. Where valves hold a fixed pressure, savings are lower. Meter the pump for a week after fitting.

example.title: One thermopac pump, one year
lines: Money: 77,578 x Rs 4.60 = Rs 3.57 lakh; payback 1.75 / 3.57 = 0.49 years
The report's 65 t used an older grid factor
example.note: Grid at CEA's FY 2025-26 factor of 0.675 kg CO2 a kWh, an estimate.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills into monthly records with CO2, so a 77,000 kWh drop shows in the months after the drive goes in. The green loan check shows what a lender asks for on a VFD loan.
